items.title: Chennai: OMR residents oppose Mamallan reservoir over flooding and wetland concerns
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. More than 50 organisations, including residents’ welfare associations (RWAs) from the Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) area, and over 1,100 citizens have petitioned Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay seeking the scrapping of the proposed Mamallan Reservoir project. The reservoir has been proposed as a source of drinking water for the OMR region, which continues to depend on private water tankers to meet part of its water needs. However, residents have opposed the project, citing concerns over flooding, damage to wetlands and its possible impacts on local livelihoods. Harsha Koda, co-founder of the Federation of OMR Residents’ Welfare Association (FOMRRA), said OMR’s residential areas are located between two important wetland systems — the Pallikaranai marsh and the Nemmeli wetlands. “This reservoir project will heighten flood risk and significantly aggravate our climate vulnerability,” he said. Residents have also raised concerns that the project could alter the drainage patterns of the Pallikaranai and Kovalam marshland catchments, which eventually drain into the sea through the Kovalam estuary.
